description: destsize - strlen(dest) is computed as size_t without a check: if dest is longer than destsize (or unterminated within it), the size wraps to a huge value and I_strcpy copies past the buffer. Should clamp, or return when strlen(dest) >= destsize.
evidence: src/universal/q_shared.cpp I_strcat; test_q_shared.py keeps destsize >= strlen(dest) for this reason. Callers not yet audited for whether any can reach it.

description: Each '*' recurses at every remaining position with no memoisation, so patterns with several '*' that fail late take exponential time (and unbounded stack). Replace with the linear backtracking glob match.
evidence: src/universal/q_shared.cpp I_stricmpwild. Callers (and whether patterns can come from the network or console) not yet identified.

description: With one null argument the result is (int)(s1 - s0): a pointer difference truncated to 32 bits, so its sign depends on the other pointer's address. Same in I_strncmp (1423B47D0) and I_stricmp (1423B48E0, inlined). Should return a fixed -1/1.
evidence: src/universal/q_shared.cpp; null-pointer inputs in test_q_shared.py match the original only because both runs use the same heap address.

description: The Store build runs Havok's Visual Debugger server: while a level's navigation volumes load (141EBE450 -> 141EBC350) it creates the visual debugger and calls serve(25001), which creates an hkBsdSocket, binds it to INADDR_ANY (every interface) on TCP port 25001 and listens; the debugger then polls for and accepts clients every frame. A listening socket in a game client, speaking Havok's VDB protocol, which was never meant to face untrusted peers.
evidence: 141EBC350 (calls 142AE2510 then 142AE2740 with 0x61A9); 142A43730 binds sin_addr 0 and listens with backlog 2; serve verified in tests/differential/test_hkVisualDebugger.py. Reached in normal play by the level-load path (not yet observed in a running game).

description: When a zone's key is missing from the built-in table, fastfile loading asks a development key server over UDP at hard-coded internal addresses 10.150.4.43 / 10.150.97.133:10019. Dead in retail networks but still opens a socket and retries; should be removed.
evidence: pseudocode 14149E620/14149E6D0/14149E870; caller 14149EAC0, gated by 141FBC390(0). Private addresses: cannot reach the internet.

description: Com_Error_ feeds a crash reporter that sends a Google Analytics event (ssl.google-analytics.com/collect, tid UA-69466650-2) with a persistent machine GUID from HKLM\\SOFTWARE\\Activision\\HardwareSurvey, writes crash_reports/*.gltn with that GUID and the Windows volume object id, and launches CrashUploader.exe through system(). Sends data off the machine without the user's knowledge; the blocking curl_easy_perform can stall error handling; system() runs whatever CrashUploader.exe is found on the search path.
evidence: pseudocode 1423B87C0 (strings), 1423B9AB0 (curl_global_init); pseudocode 1423B8BA0 (gltn writer, system call), 1423B9DE0 (report); call chain Com_Error_ 142210B90 -> 1423B9F70; report via 1423F1F80 -> 1423B9DE0. docs/network.md section 3.

description: A datagram received on an IPv6 socket leaves the sender's address where WSARecvFrom put it (sockaddr_in6 layout: family, port and flow info in the first 8 bytes) instead of moving sin6_addr to the start as the reset path does, and m_family is never set from the received address: the caller gets a wrong IPv6 peer address. IPv4 is handled correctly.
evidence: src/libs/DemonWareGDK/bdPlatform/bdPlatformSocket/bdPlatformSocket-xboxone.cpp receiveFrom (success, AF_INET6) against its reset path; tests/differential/test_bdPlatformSocket.py covers both. Reachable whenever Demonware uses an IPv6 socket.

description: Copies ai_addrlen bytes of each result into a 16-byte stack sockaddr_in without checking the length: a longer address would overflow the stack. The hints ask for AF_INET only, so Winsock returns 16-byte addresses today. The bdSockAddrs it fills also never get m_family set.
evidence: src/libs/DemonWareGDK/bdPlatform/bdPlatformSocket/bdPlatformSocket-xboxone.cpp getHostByName; the faithful test uses ai_addrlen <= 16. No current input reaches the overflow.

description: For AF_INET6, a failed WSASocketA is logged and then setsockopt(IPV6_V6ONLY) is still called on the invalid handle, which fails and logs a second, misleading error before returning -1. For AF_INET a failed socket() is not logged at all.
evidence: src/libs/DemonWareGDK/bdPlatform/bdPlatformSocket/bdPlatformSocket-xboxone.cpp create; covered by test_bdPlatformSocket.py (sockets that come back INVALID_SOCKET).

description: On WSAENOTCONN it calls checkSocketException, drops the result and falls through into the WSAEMSGSIZE case, so a receive on an unconnected socket reports BD_NET_MSG_SIZE. send handles the same error properly (BD_NET_CONNECTION_RESET or BD_NET_NOT_CONNECTED). A missing return in the original switch.
evidence: src/libs/DemonWareGDK/bdPlatform/bdPlatformSocket/bdPlatformStreamSocket-xboxone.cpp receive; covered by test_bdPlatformStreamSocket.py (error 10057). Reachable when the lobby connection drops before it is established.

description: Always builds an AF_INET sockaddr from the address's first four bytes, whatever m_family says, so a TCP connection to an IPv6 address (on a socket create made with AF_INET6) can never succeed.
evidence: src/libs/DemonWareGDK/bdPlatform/bdPlatformSocket/bdPlatformStreamSocket-xboxone.cpp connect; covered by test_bdPlatformStreamSocket.py (all families). Reachable only if Demonware is given an IPv6 server address.

description: r_refreshRate is registered with the domain [1, 240] (default 60, latched). Dvar_SetVariant (1423A21C0) refuses a value outside a dvar's domain and keeps the old one, so nothing above 240 Hz can be set: the first-run hardware detection (141DA9620) sets the fastest mode's rate and is refused on a >240 Hz monitor (r_refreshRate stays 60), choosing 360 in the menu or console is refused, and the fullscreen swap chain (141DA7A00) picks the mode closest to the value that stuck. Mode enumeration has no limit and com_maxfps goes to 1000, so the domain is the whole cap.
evidence: tests/enhanced/test_refresh_rate.py test_refresh_rate_domain (the original registers 60, 1, 240); Dvar_SetVariant 1423A21C0 pseudocode (Dvar_ValueInDomain false -> message, value kept). Every player on a >240 Hz monitor hits it.

description: Looks at only the first 128 entries of the monitor's mode list (min(dx_modeCount, 128)). The list is sorted smallest size first and DXGI_ENUM_MODES_SCALING makes it long, so on monitors with more than 128 modes the largest resolutions (usually the native one) get no refresh rates in the settings menu.
evidence: tests/enhanced/test_refresh_rate.py test_native_mode_past_128 (original lists nothing for 2560x1440 at indexes 135..139); 1420E7490 cmovle with 0x80. Reachable whenever a monitor reports more than 128 modes.

description: The display-mode comparator never returns 0: for equal sizes it returns -1 if a's rate is lower, else 1, so two modes with the same rate each compare greater than the other. qsort's contract is broken (the order of equal-rate duplicates is unspecified); 141DAA790 merges such duplicates right after, so nothing visible follows from it today.
evidence: tests/differential/test_r_init.py (equal-rate pairs return 1 both ways in the original); 141DAA73E..141DAA789.

description: On AMD (vendor 0x1002) with r_vsync on, the present path sleeps Sleep(1000 / r_refreshRate - 2) ms, truncated, before every present: a frame pacer built on the requested rate rather than the mode actually in use, at Sleep's coarse timer granularity, adding input latency. Not decompiled yet.
evidence: 141D46720 pseudocode (Dvar_GetFloat(r_refreshRate), -1000.0/x, Sleep). Every AMD player with vsync on runs it.
